artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain representing the reference configuration of an elastic body, and let $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}\to[0,\infty]$ be a stored-energy density satisfying the standard assumptions of nonlinear elastostatics: frame indifference $W(RF)=W(F)$ for all $R\in SO(3)$, material symmetry, $W(F)\to\infty$ as $\det F\to 0^+$, $W(F)=\infty$ if $\det F\le 0$, and suitable polyconvexity/coercivity ensuring existence of minimizers in the classical pure elastic setting.

For a deformation $y:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^3$ in a space of special functions of bounded variation (so that the approximate gradient $Dy$ exists a.e. and the jump set $S_y$ is a countably $\mathcal{H}^{2}$-rectifiable subset of $\Omega$), and for a surface energy density $\psi:\mathbb{R}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3\times S^2\to [0,\infty)$ (depending on the one-sided traces $y^\pm$ and the unit normal $\nu_y$ to $S_y$), define the Griffith-type variational fracture energy
$$
I(y)=\int_{\Omega} W(Dy)\,dx+\int_{S_y}\psi(y^+,y^-,\nu_y)\,d\mathcal{H}^{2},
$$
subject to prescribed Dirichlet boundary data on a portion of $\partial\Omega$.

Clarify the precise relationship between the variational fracture model based on minimizing (or finding local minimizers / stable critical points of) the functional $I$ and (i) classical Griffith fracture mechanics, and (ii) the variational theory of nonlinear elastostatics (where only the bulk term is present). In particular, address the following:

(a) Fracture initiation: characterize, in terms of $W$, $\psi$, and the loading, the conditions under which a globally stable elastic equilibrium $y$ with $S_y=\emptyset$ ceases to be a local minimizer of $I$, and identify the mechanism by which a nontrivial jump set first appears.

(b) Stability: give intrinsic criteria distinguishing global minimizers, local minimizers, and merely stationary configurations of $I$, and relate these to stability notions in classical fracture mechanics (e.g., Griffith's energy-release criterion) and to quasi-static evolutions.

(c) Local minimizers vs. global minimizers: determine whether and in what sense the local-minimization formulation of $I$ is the correct selection principle, and how the resulting solutions compare with the classical solutions of nonlinear elastostatics in regimes where no fracture occurs.
artifact.status_search_result: The relationship between variational (Francfort–Marigo / Ambrosio–De Giorgi type) fracture models and classical Griffith fracture mechanics and nonlinear elastostatics is a recognized open problem area. Substantial partial results exist (existence of global minimizers in SBV/GSBD by Dal Maso, Francfort, Toader and others; quasi-static evolutions; convergence to Griffith in special regimes), but a complete clarification covering initiation, stability, and local minimizers in genuinely nonlinear elasticity remains open.

status_evidence.title: Francfort–Marigo variational fracture model
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces the energy I(y)=∫W(Dy)+surface term and proves existence of global minimizers; raises questions about local minimizers and relation to Griffith.
status_evidence.claim: The variational formulation and its relation to classical Griffith theory is an active research topic with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: Dal Maso–Francfort–Toader, quasi-static crack growth in nonlinear elasticity
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of quasi-static evolutions for nonlinear elastic fracture, leaving open questions about stability and local minimizers.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist; full clarification including initiation and local minimizers remains open.
